quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver wants to pass you, slow down. This gives them enough space in front of your vehicle to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed on the side with the solid yellow line.
Allowed on the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed on the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When one yellow line is broken and one is solid, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. The solid line side is a no-passing zone.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and allow plenty of time for travel.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction due to water on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep a steady speed to improve traction.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your tires lose contact with the road and ride on water (hydroplaning), slow down gradually and do not use the brakes. This happens even at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help others see you, even if they don't help your visibility much.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time become slower.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes worse.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines are doubled in this work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns of low overhead clearance ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.
All large trucks have air brakes for quick stops.
They are easier to maneuver than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much longer to stop. A passenger vehicle traveling at 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.explanation: In rainy conditions, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that a red light is coming soon. Slow down and get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Some crossings do not have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly return to the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly return to the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Slow down, check for traffic, and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area.

questions.question: Why use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Bad weather makes it hard for other drivers to see you. Use your headlights to make your vehicle more visible. If you need windshield wipers, you must also use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: It is okay because bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, stop and inch forward until you can see in both directions.

questions.question: When can you drive around railroad crossing gates?
questions.explanation: Always stop at railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train sounds. Never drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. Stay far behind the vehicle in front of you, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to help balance the vehicle. Steer toward the direction of the skid to regain control.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up your right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up your right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Always look at what is happening at the intersection. Give up your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that when turning left at a green light, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should they do?

options.text: They will drive the same as usual.
They can drive faster because they are more alert.
They should calm down and focus before driving.
They should call a friend while driving to talk about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should calm down and focus before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can make you unable to drive safely. When you are worried, angry, or upset, your mind is not on driving. Calm yourself and focus before you start the engine.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead helps you:
questions.explanation: Looking ahead gives you time to brake or change lanes safely. You can drive safer, use less fuel, and help traffic move smoothly.
